newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Canada minister to attend HK assembly investiture.
newsitem.headline: Canada minister to attend HK assembly investiture.

text.p: Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Monday he would attend the swearing-in of Hong Kong's controversial unelected legislature that China is installing to replace an elected parliament after the handover.

Axworthy told reporters he would attend the Provisional Legislature's investiture soon after the Monday midnight handover, despite a boycott by British and U.S. ministers who oppose China's disbandment of the elected assembly.
Axworthy said Canada had an important stake in Hong Kong, and intended to maintain a close relationship with the new Hong Kong administration led by Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa.
"At the same time, we want to convey that Canada expects China to live up to its commitments regarding Hong Kong's autonomy, its institutions and way of life," Axworthy said.
He said he had met Chief Secretary Anson Chan, the territory's top civil servant, on Monday and would meet Tung on Wednesday and Democratic Party head Martin Lee on July 1.
Britain's Prince Charles will formally hand Hong Kong back to Chinese President Jiang Zemin at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday, marking the end of more than 150 years of British rule.
